correctness.rationale: Exact 27-state transfer coding counts every outer, spoke and inner step-two bond once for n>=5. Five supplied integral dual potentials certify 1215 explicit nonnegative transition reduced costs; all periods of the six explicit color-word witnesses divide twenty and each attains its claimed affine branch. Affine interpolation and endpoint occupancy bounds prove the universal all-n lower bound. Periodic tiling yields equality for all n divisible by twenty; a bounded seam cost yields O(1/n) for arbitrary n. Secant derivatives prove the occupancy laws. Standalone checker run from its actual package path verified 1215 inequalities, six witness energy counts and eleven independent n20 min-plus optimality checks. No unproved infinite step relies on enumeration.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2000 next-nearest-neighbor strip paper concerns degree-five square ladder strips without a magnetic field; inspected 2009 and 2010 works establish broad magnetic Potts transfer frameworks on different graph families, not evaluated GP(n,2) magnetic thresholds. The directly comparable complete GP(10,2) field diagram is a single ten-cell case with critical field 3/2 between 0 and3; it neither covers nor implies the new infinite-size split 5/4 and7/4, nor exact equality across all multiples of twenty. An unindexed earlier equivalent computation is still a priority risk.
residual_risks: Prior work might encode the same minimum-cycle-mean evaluation implicitly or in unindexed material.
The broad polynomial frameworks could yield the formula after a nontrivial new specialization; no claim is made that mere use of transfer methods is original.

value.rationale: Exact infinite-family zero-temperature response identifies five sharp physically meaningful field thresholds and six favored-spin density plateaux, with a nontrivial commensurability condition for exact finite-size realization. The 5/4 and 7/4 split is absent from the known ten-cell diagram. A rigorous finite dual-certificate method turns the full 27-state min-plus optimization into an independently reproducible universal result. It resolves an explicit magnetic limit, not a routine evaluation of one arbitrary small graph; no thermodynamic finite-temperature phase transition is asserted.
